name: Instinct MI250X
notes: Launched Nov 2021. Two GCDs in one OAM package. BF16/INT8 383 are dense (CDNA2 has no sparsity, no FP8). TDP 500W (560W peak). 8192-bit bus. Scale-up: 8 Infinity Fabric links x 100 GB/s = 800 GB/s peak aggregate (whitepaper). The 8 stacks come from the whitepaper block diagram (8 x 1024-bit), not from text.

name: Instinct MI300X
notes: Launched Dec 2023. Dense values (footnote MI300-18); structured sparsity is 2x (BF16 2614.9, FP8/INT8 5229.8). Headline 5.3 TB/s; footnote MI300-05A gives exact 5.325 TB/s (8192b x 5.2 Gbps). 8 stacks x 24GB (whitepaper). TBP 750W. The product page lists 8 IF links x 128 GB/s, but the whitepaper says 7 links form the 8-GPU mesh, so 7x128 = 896.

name: Instinct MI325X
notes: Launched Oct 2024. Datasheet dense values; sparse is 2x. 8 stacks x 32GB. Scale-up: 7 x 128 GB/s. TBP 1000W.

name: Instinct MI355X
notes: Launched Jun 2025. The product page rounds (BF16 2.5 PF, FP8 5 PF, INT8 5 POPS); exact values are the 8-GPU platform brochure divided by 8. Sparse is 2x. The brochure's OCP-FP8 dense cell (40.5312 PF) looks like a typo for 40.2656. MXFP4/MXFP6 10.1 PF. 8 stacks of 12-Hi HBM3E (CDNA4 whitepaper). Scale-up: 7 x 153.6 GB/s. TBP 1400W (MI350X is the 1000W sibling). FP4 dense = MXFP4 80.5 PFLOPS platform brochure / 8.

name: M2 (base)
notes: Apple states 100GB/s unified memory bandwidth and up to 24GB. The newsroom text does not name the DRAM type; LPDDR5 is from WWDC22 keynote and secondary sources. Apple publishes no BF16/FP16 TFLOPS, so blank. Neural Engine 15.8 TOPS (precision unstated). GPU up to 10 cores. No TDP published. Not HBM. memory_gb records the measured 8 GB configuration; Apple publishes configurations up to 24 GB.

name: Gaudi 2
notes: Launched May 2022. Bandwidth: Intel gives 2.45 TB/s; the Gaudi 3 whitepaper table gives 2.46. BF16/FP8 MME TFLOPS are from the Gaudi 3 whitepaper comparison table (no sparsity on Gaudi). Stack count and INT8 matrix rate not published. Scale-up: 24x100GbE RoCE = 600 GB/s bidirectional (21 ports all-to-all in 8-card board). TDP 600W (HL-225H).

name: Gaudi 3 (HL-325L OAM)
notes: Whitepaper Rev.3 (Jul 2025) gives 1678 TFLOPS BF16/FP8 MME; 2024 launch materials said 1835 (1.8 PF). MME FP16 is only 459 TFLOPS, so BF16 and FP16 differ. 8 x 16GB HBM2e. INT8 matrix rate not published. Scale-up: 24x200GbE = 1200 GB/s bidirectional (21 ports OAM-to-OAM). TDP 900W OAM (PCIe card 600W).

name: A100 SXM 40GB
notes: Datasheet gives dense | sparse: BF16 312 | 624*, INT8 624 | 1248*. No FP8 on Ampere. Whitepaper: 5 active HBM2 stacks.

name: A100 SXM 80GB
notes: Dense values shown; sparse is 2x. TDP 400W (HGX custom-thermal SKU up to 500W). hbm_stacks is blank because it is not stated for the 80GB part (likely 5, same 5120-bit bus).

name: A10G
notes: No nvidia.com page (AWS-specific part). Source is the co-branded NVIDIA/AWS datasheet on AWS's site. Dense | sparse: BF16 70 | 140*, INT8 140 | 280*. No FP8. PCIe only.

name: B200 (HGX B200 per GPU)
notes: 8-GPU totals divided by 8. HGX lists BF16 36 PF, FP8 72 PF, INT8 72 POPS, all sparse; dense per GPU = 2250/4500/4500. 180GB per GPU is from the PCF summary. Bandwidth: DGX B200 gives 64 TB/s (8000/GPU); the HGX PCF summary gives 62 TB/s (7750/GPU). NVLink5 1.8 TB/s per GPU. TDP: PCF says configurable up to 1000W. HBM stacks not published. FP4 dense 9000 = HGX B200 FP4 72 PFLOPS dense / 8 (https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/hgx/).

name: GB200 (per Blackwell GPU)
notes: Superchip (1 Grace + 2 GPUs) values divided by 2: 372GB, 16 TB/s, BF16 10 PF, FP8 20 PF, INT8 20 POPS (sparse; the page footnote says dense is 1/2), NVLink 3.6 TB/s. Per-GPU TDP not published. Grace LPDDR5X: up to 480GB at up to 512 GB/s per superchip. HBM stacks not published. FP4 dense 10000 = GB200 NVL72 FP4 1440 PFLOPS sparse / 72 / 2 (dense is half of sparse per page footnote).

name: GH200 Grace Hopper (HBM3 96GB)
notes: Datasheet gives sparse | dense explicitly: BF16 1979* | 990, FP8 3958* | 1979, INT8 3958* | 1979. NVLink-C2C 900 GB/s total (450 per direction; CPU-GPU, not scale-up, so scaleup is blank). LPDDR5X up to 480GB; bandwidth up to 384 GB/s (datasheet table) vs up to 500 GB/s (datasheet text/whitepaper). tdp_w is superchip module power, configurable 450-1000W. HBM stacks not published.

name: GH200 Grace Hopper (HBM3e 144GB)
notes: Same compute as the HBM3 variant. Bandwidth up to 4.9 TB/s. NVLink-C2C 900 GB/s total. LPDDR5X up to 480GB at 384-500 GB/s (sources disagree). Module power 450-1000W configurable. Announced Aug 2023.

name: H100 PCIe
notes: The product brief (nvidia.com) gives memory, 350W max TDP (300-350 configurable) and the 600 GB/s NVLink bridge. FLOPS come from NVIDIA's datasheet on a partner site (the nvidia.com copy is retired): BF16 1513*, FP8 3026*, INT8 3026* (*sparsity); dense = half. Whitepaper: 5 HBM2e stacks. nvidia.com/h100 now shows H100 NVL (94GB, 3.9 TB/s) instead.

name: H100 SXM
notes: Page lists BF16 1979*, FP8 3958*, INT8 3958* (*with sparsity); dense = half. HBM3 and 5 stacks come from the Hopper whitepaper (NVIDIA document, partner-hosted copy). The whitepaper's preliminary 3000 GB/s was superseded by the datasheet's 3350. TDP up to 700W configurable.

name: H200 SXM
notes: Datasheet lists BF16 1979, FP8 3958, INT8 3958, all marked with sparsity; dense = half. HBM stack count not published. TDP up to 700W configurable. Announced Nov 2023.

name: L4
notes: Datasheet: BF16 242*, FP8 485*, INT8 485* ('*Shown with sparsity. 1/2 lower without'); dense = half. 192-bit GDDR6. PCIe Gen4 x16 only (no NVLink), so scaleup is blank.

name: T4
notes: Turing has no BF16 or FP8: the 65 is the FP16 mixed-precision Tensor figure (dense; no sparsity on Turing). INT8 130 TOPS. PCIe Gen3 only, no NVLink. Datasheet (verified) says '300 GB/sec'. The theoretical 256-bit x 10 Gbps = 320 GB/s; the official figure is kept.

name: V100 SXM2 32GB
notes: Volta has no BF16: the 125 is the FP16 mixed-precision Tensor figure (dense; Volta has no sparsity). No FP8. INT8 tensor TOPS not published. NVLink 300 GB/s. hbm_stacks is blank because the whitepaper states 4 HBM2 stacks only for the 16GB part; the 32GB part likely also has 4 (same 4096-bit bus), but that is not stated.

name: TPU v4
notes: Doc: 32 GiB (=34.36 GB decimal) HBM2 at 1200 GBps; 275 TFLOPS peak listed as 'bf16 or int8'. The 4 HBM stacks and the ICI figure (6 links x 50 GB/s = 300 GB/s, direction unstated) come from the ISCA'23 paper (arXiv 2304.01433), not the docs page. TDP blank: the paper lists N.A., and the doc gives only measured power (min/mean/max 90/170/192 W). Production 2020; Cloud announcement 2021.

name: TPU v5e
notes: Doc lists '800 GiBps'. Strict conversion is 859 GB/s, but v6e's doubled bandwidth (1638 = 2x819.2) implies the intended value is 819 GB/s. HBM generation is not stated by Google. ICI 400 GB/s is bidirectional per chip (4 ports, 2D torus). No FP8 or TDP published. Announced Aug 2023.

name: TPU v5p
notes: Doc: 95 GiB (=102.0 GB decimal) at 2765 GBps. Doc lists FP8 459 = BF16 (no FP8 speedup). INT8 918 TOPS is SECONDARY (The Register 2023-12-06: https://www.theregister.com/2023/12/06/google_unveils_tpu_v5p_pods/) and is not on Google docs. ICI in the doc is 1200 GB/s bidirectional; the blog says 4800 Gbps (=600 GB/s, likely per direction). HBM generation not stated. No TDP published. Announced Dec 2023.

name: TPU v6e (Trillium)
notes: Doc: 32 GB at 1638 GBps; 918 TFLOPS bf16; 1836 TOPS int8. ICI 800 GB/s bidirectional (4 ports). HBM generation not stated. No FP8 or TDP published. Announced May 2024; GA Dec 2024.
